rules.holds: An offer holds a player when it contains him: he is among the players it sends or gets, whatever else it also moves.
rules.get: get[key] lists up to 5 indexes into offers, best first (the owner's tier-weighted lens score, then fewer players), of the offers whose get holds that player; an offer dominated by a better one that sends and gets a subset of its players is left out. No such offer: {reason}.
rules.send: send[key] maps each partner to the index of the best offer that team has whose send holds that player. No offer with any partner: {reason}.
rules.pairs: pairs lists each pair of the owner's own players (sorted by key) that at least one offer sends together, with the best such offer across all teams; a pair no offer sends is absent.

reasons.namesake: his team is named after him, so he is never asked for (rules.namesake of trade_offers.json)
reasons.unpriced: he has no rest-of-season value (under 2 games left), so he is never sent or asked for
reasons.no_gain_for_you: no package that holds him lifts the owner's rest-of-season lineup by rules.min_gain
reasons.no_gain_for_him: every package that lifts the owner leaves the partner perceiving a gain of at most rules.min_perc, or leaves a side unable to field a lineup
reasons.lens_gate: every package that he would perceive as a gain gives the partner no lens gain, or a tier-weighted lens score of 0 or less (rules.partner of trade_offers.json)
reasons.no_legal_drop: every remaining package leaves a side over the roster cap with nobody legal to release, or costs the owner points once his room is counted

rules.reason_order: The reason is the first of rules.order that holds, read in the order the search tests a package: the owner's floor, then the partner's perceived gain, then the lens gate, then the roster rooms.
